---
title: "Tutorial: re-docking a 7-mer peptide"
---

{{< include /_includes/adcp-1.0-banner.md >}}

This tutorial re-docks a known peptide into its native receptor: a pseudophosphorylated Smad1
peptide into the TPR domain of CHIP ([PDB 3Q47](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/3Q47)).

**You will learn to:**

- generate a target file for docking in a box defined by the known peptide
- run ADCP to re-dock the peptide
- understand the output of an ADCP docking run

**Prerequisites:** ADFRsuite 1.0 installed with `ADFRsuite-1.0/bin` on your `PATH`, and the
[tutorial data](https://ccsb.scripps.edu/adcp/download/1063/) downloaded
(see [Tutorials](tutorials.qmd)).

## 1. Convert PDB files to PDBQT files

PDBQT is the file format of the AutoDock programs. It adds two columns to the PDB format: the
partial charge and the AutoDock atom type.

We start from two separate PDB files for the receptor and the peptide, split from the
[3Q47 entry](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/3Q47). Both contain only protein atoms.

Unzip the data and go to the directory for this tutorial:

```bash
unzip ADCP_tutorial_data.zip
cd ADCP_tutorial_data/3Q47
```

Add hydrogens to both files with [reduce](http://kinemage.biochem.duke.edu/software/reduce.php)
(included in ADFRsuite):

```bash
reduce 3Q47_rec.pdb > 3Q47_recH.pdb
reduce 3Q47_pep.pdb > 3Q47_pepH.pdb
```

Convert the protonated PDB files into PDBQT files with `prepare_receptor` and `prepare_ligand`:

```bash
prepare_receptor -r 3Q47_recH.pdb
prepare_ligand -l 3Q47_pepH.pdb
```

## 2. Generate the target file

A target file is a zipped file with everything needed for docking with ADFR and ADCP. It can be
generated from the command line or a GUI.

```bash
agfr -r 3Q47_recH.pdbqt -l 3Q47_pepH.pdbqt -asv 1.1 -o 3Q47
```

This puts the docking box around the given peptide with 4 Å padding. If you do not know the
peptide binding site, see the [agfrgui tutorials](/software/agfr/tutorials.qmd).

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-r` | the receptor file (required) |
| `-l` | the ligand file |
| `-asv` | AutoSite version, 1.0 or 1.1 (default 1.0 when `-asv` is not given) |
| `-o` | name for the target file |

**Details.** `agfr` positions and sizes the docking box over the receptor pocket(s) where the
ligand will be docked, and computes affinity maps for a list of AutoDock4 atom types. The maps are
calculated by AutoGrid4.

- **Box.** The box can be set in several ways with `-b/--boxMode`. Here agfr uses the bounding box
  of the known ligand (`-l/--ligand`), with 4 Å of padding added on every side. Change the padding
  with `-P/--padding`.
- **Output.** The target file (`.trg`) is saved under the name given by `-o/--output`; without
  it, a unique descriptive name is created. It contains the affinity maps, translational points
  for placing the ligand at sensible positions in the box, and metadata about the grid size,
  position and spacing, the receptor atoms involved and the maps. Inspect it with the `about`
  command.
- **Pockets.** The translational points are computed by AutoSite, which clusters high-affinity
  grid points into potential binding pockets. `-p/--pocketMode` sets how multiple clusters are
  handled; when it is omitted, as here, all clusters are merged into one set of translational
  points.
- **Atom types.** By default maps are computed for all AutoDock4 atom types. Restrict them with
  `-m/--mapTypes` for smaller files and faster runs, but the target file then cannot dock
  ligands with atom types it has no map for.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## 3. Dock the peptide from its sequence

```bash
adcp -t 3Q47.trg -s npisdvd -N 20 -n 1000000 -o 3Q47_redocking -ref 3Q47_pepH.pdb
```

`adcp` detects the available cores and uses all of them by default. Here it runs 20 independent
searches (`-N, --nbRuns 20`), each with up to 1,000,000 evaluations of the scoring function
(`-n, --numSteps`). By default `adcp` runs 50 searches of 2.5 million evaluations each. Harder
docking problems need more searches to raise the chance of finding the best pose (the global
minimum of the scoring function).

The run writes:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `3Q47_redocking_ranked_*.pdb` | final solutions, ranked after clustering |
| `3Q47_redocking_*.pdb` | the Monte Carlo trajectory of each replica |
| `3Q47_redocking_*.out` | detailed output of each replica |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Notes
- The search is stochastic: docking the same peptide into the same target twice can give
  different results with different random seeds. The energy landscape is the same in both runs;
  if both find its global minimum they give the same solution, whatever path the search took.
  Searches trapped in local minima give different poses. Setting the seed (`--seed`) makes a
  run reproducible for a given version of the code.
- In general, run 100 replicas with 1 million steps per amino acid, starting from a mixture of
  extended and helical conformations.
:::

## Review note (prototype only)
The CCSB text said each search uses "up to 2,500,000 evaluations (`-n, --numSteps 2500000`)",
which does not match the command (`-n 1000000`). Changed to 1,000,000 here.
:::
